description: Implement all services (storage.ts, dataset.ts, gps.ts, audio.ts, alerts.ts) and create a wired-up App.tsx that integrates them with the AlertEngine loop. Independent of FEAT-003/004 in terms of UI, but provides the full business logic layer.
steps: Step 1 — Create `src/services/storage.ts`. Use `@capacitor/preferences` (import `{ Preferences }` from '@capacitor/preferences'). Implement: `loadSettings(): Promise<AppSettings>` — reads key 'settings', parses JSON, merges with defaults (tiposAtivos: ['RF','RM','SR','SC','PRv','LOM'], vozAtiva: true, volume: 0.8, manterTela: true, avisarAcimaLimite: false); `saveSettings(s: AppSettings): Promise<void>` — JSON.stringify and store; `loadUserPoints(): Promise<UserPoint[]>` — reads key 'userPoints', parses JSON, returns [] on empty/error; `saveUserPoints(pts: UserPoint[]): Promise<void>`; `hasSeenDisclaimer(): Promise<boolean>` — reads key 'disclaimerSeen'; `markDisclaimerSeen(): Promise<void>`. NEVER store or log coordinates.

Step 2 — Create `src/services/dataset.ts`. Implement: `loadDataset(): Promise<DatasetJson>` — imports base dataset from `../data/radares_pr.json` (static JSON import, bundled into APK); `mergeDataset(base: DatasetJson, userPoints: UserPoint[]): DatasetJson` — returns a new DatasetJson with userPoints appended to base.pontos as [lat, lon, tipo, limite] tuples, preserving meta; `validateImport(raw: unknown, maxBytes: number): { ok: true; data: DatasetJson } | { ok: false; error: string }` — checks: (1) raw is object with meta and pontos array, (2) pontos entries are 4-element arrays, (3) lat in range -26.7 to -22.5, lon in range -54.6 to -48.0, tipo is string key in known set, limite is number, (4) JSON.stringify(raw).length <= maxBytes (use 5_000_000 bytes = 5 MB). Reject silently with error message on any failure — never throw to caller.

Step 3 — Create `src/services/gps.ts`. Import `BackgroundGeolocation` from '@capacitor-community/background-geolocation'. Implement a class or module with: `startGps(onPosition: (pos: {lat: number, lon: number, velKmh: number, heading: number | null}) => void): Promise<void>` — calls `BackgroundGeolocation.addWatcher({ backgroundMessage: 'Monitorando radares', backgroundTitle: 'Radares PR', requestPermissions: true, stale: false, distanceFilter: 0 }, (location, error) => { if (error || !location) return; onPosition({ lat: location.latitude, lon: location.longitude, velKmh: (location.speed ?? 0) * 3.6, heading: location.bearing ?? null }); })` and stores the watcher ID; `stopGps(): Promise<void>` — calls `BackgroundGeolocation.removeWatcher({ id: watcherId })` and clears ID; `isMockMode: boolean` toggle; `startMock(onPosition, intervalMs = 1000): void` — iterates through a hardcoded array of 20 coordinates simulating approach to a radar point (choose coordinates near a known LOM or RF in radares_pr.json, spaced ~100 m apart at ~80 km/h equivalent), calls onPosition every intervalMs via setInterval; `stopMock(): void` — clears the interval. Mock coordinates must NOT be logged or stored. Mock should be enableable via a compile-time env var `import.meta.env.VITE_MOCK_GPS === 'true'`.

Step 4 — Create `src/services/audio.ts`. Implement audio using the Web Audio API (AudioContext) for bipe/alarm sounds, and `@capacitor-community/text-to-speech` for voice. Functions: `async function playBip(): Promise<void>` — creates a short 880 Hz sine-wave beep (0.3 s) using AudioContext; `async function playAlarm(): Promise<void>` — creates a louder repeating tone pattern (3 cycles of 440→880 Hz, ~1.5 s) using AudioContext; `async function speak(text: string, volume: number): Promise<void>` — calls `TextToSpeech.speak({ text, lang: 'pt-BR', rate: 1.0, pitch: 1.0, volume, category: 'alarm' })`, catches error and logs a non-sensitive message (no coordinates) without rethrowing; `async function playAlert(som: 'aviso' | 'alarme', mensagem: string, vozAtiva: boolean, volume: number): Promise<void>` — plays bip (som=aviso) or alarm (som=alarme) first, then calls speak() if vozAtiva, falling back to alarm-only if speak throws. AudioContext should be created lazily on first use and reused. Note: the `category: 'alarm'` in TTS speak() and the AudioContext both help Android route to the alarm/navigation audio stream; the actual Android AudioFocus is managed by the plugin — no separate native call is needed from JS.

Step 5 — Create `src/services/alerts.ts`. Import `AlertEngine` from '../lib/alertEngine', `AppSettings` and `UserPoint` from '../types', `playAlert` from './audio'. Implement class `AlertDispatcher` with: constructor that accepts `dataset: DatasetJson`, `settings: AppSettings`, and `onVisualAlert: (event: AlertEvent) => void`; creates `this.engine = new AlertEngine(dataset, { tiposAtivos: settings.tiposAtivos })` internally; method `handle(pos: {lat: number, lon: number, velKmh: number, heading: number | null}): void` — calls `this.engine.atualizar(pos)`, iterates events (max 1 per call), calls `playAlert(ev.som, ev.mensagem, settings.vozAtiva, settings.volume)`, calls `onVisualAlert(ev)` only if `ev.visual` is set and (settings.avisarAcimaLimite || !ev.acimaDoLimite) — actually: always fire visual alert, but pass acimaDoLimite info through so UI can decide; method `recreate(dataset: DatasetJson, settings: AppSettings)` — replaces this.engine with a new AlertEngine (needed when settings change). The dispatcher must not duplicate alerts — the engine already deduplicates; do not add extra state on top.

Step 6 — Update `src/App.tsx` to wire all services together. App state: `isMonitoring (boolean)`, `currentPos ({lat, lon, velKmh, heading}|null)`, `nextEvent (AlertEvent|null)`, `visualAlert (AlertEvent|null)`, `settings (AppSettings)`, `userPoints (UserPoint[])`, `dataset (DatasetJson)`, `disclaimerSeen (boolean)`. On mount: load settings, userPoints, dataset, disclaimerSeen from storage; merge dataset. Create AlertDispatcher with onVisualAlert = (ev) => setVisualAlert(ev). On Start: call gps.startGps((pos) => { setCurrentPos(pos); dispatcher.handle(pos); }); activate keep-awake if settings.manterTela. On Stop: call gps.stopGps(); deactivate keep-awake. Expose all state and handlers as props or context to child components. Render placeholder '
Radares PR loading...
' — real UI comes in FEAT-003.
Step 7 — Run `npm run build`. Fix any TypeScript errors before marking this FEAT complete.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` exits 0 with no TypeScript errors
`src/services/storage.ts` exports loadSettings, saveSettings, loadUserPoints, saveUserPoints, hasSeenDisclaimer, markDisclaimerSeen — all returning Promises
`src/services/dataset.ts` exports loadDataset, mergeDataset, validateImport — validateImport rejects lat outside -26.7 to -22.5 and lon outside -54.6 to -48.0
`src/services/gps.ts` exports startGps, stopGps, startMock, stopMock — mock mode triggers onPosition callback with non-null lat/lon
`src/services/audio.ts` exports playAlert — if TTS throws, falls back to alarm sound without rethrowing
`src/services/alerts.ts` exports AlertDispatcher with handle() and recreate() methods
No user coordinates are passed to Preferences.set() or console.log() anywhere in the services
verification: Run `npm run build` — must exit 0 with no TypeScript errors
findings: 1. @capacitor-community/background-geolocation@1.3.1 does not have a JS/ESM entry point — it is a pure Capacitor native plugin. The correct import pattern is `registerPlugin<BackgroundGeolocationPlugin>('BackgroundGeolocation')` from '@capacitor/core', with types imported from '@capacitor-community/background-geolocation'. Importing the package directly as a default import fails at TypeScript level. 2. The plugin's callback signature is `(position?: Location, error?: CallbackError) => void` (both optional), not `(location, error)` with implicit any. Explicit types are required since tsconfig has strict mode. 3. dataset.ts loadDataset() is synchronous (static JSON import bundled by Vite) — declared return type is DatasetJson not Promise<DatasetJson>. App.tsx calls it synchronously in the init effect. 4. AppState interface is exported from App.tsx for FEAT-003 UI components to consume via props or context. 5. `npm run build` exited 0, `npx cap sync` exited 0. All 4 Capacitor plugins registered correctly in Android.
